items.summary: Proto types in encounter service.go Input/Output types (not just orchestrator.go)
items.details: orchestrators/encounter/service.go:7 imports pb and uses pb.MonsterType in MonsterCombatState (line 459), pb.CombatAbilityId in ActivateCombatAbilityInput (line 511), and pb.ActionId in ExecuteActionInput (line 535). The first reviewer pass noted proto types in the orchestrator implementation (~50 pb. refs in orchestrator.go), but the Input/Output types in service.go are also contaminated. Any caller of the Service interface must also import pb.

items.summary: entities package imports and constructs proto messages
items.details: entities/entity_state.go and entities/encounter_state_builder.go contain full proto construction functions (ToEntityStateProto, BuildEncounterStateData, CombatStateToProto). These belong in the handler converter layer. entities/encounter_events.go embeds *dnd5ev1alpha1.EncounterStateData, *dnd5ev1alpha1.EntityState, *dnd5ev1alpha1.CombatState as json:"-" fields in 9 event structs. entities/room.go stores apiv1alpha1.GridType (a proto enum) directly on the Room entity struct.

items.summary: RoomData stored as interface{} in EncounterData and input types
items.details: encounters/repository.go: EncounterData.RoomData, SaveInput.RoomData, and UpdateInput.RoomData are all typed as interface{} with a comment 'Temporarily using interface{} until spatial is fixed'. The orchestrator uses type assertions at every access point. This makes the repository and orchestrator brittle and disables type checking for room data.

items.summary: DEPRECATED fields in EncounterData still present during migration
items.details: encounters/repository.go: EncounterData has both Monsters []*monster.Data + CharacterHP map[string]int (DEPRECATED comments) AND Entities map[string]*entities.EntityStateData (the new unified approach). Both are present simultaneously. There is no migration path or deprecation deadline visible.

items.summary: SandboxRoom service has interface but no implementation wired
items.details: services/sandboxroom/service.go defines a Service interface with 11 methods covering room generation, spatial queries, and entity management. There is no orchestrator, handler, or server wiring for this service. It is a declared interface with no implementation path visible.

items.summary: Three Position types with different int/float64 signatures
items.details: entities.Position uses float64 X,Y,Z. dungeon.Position uses int X,Y,Z. apiv1alpha1.Position (proto) uses float64 X,Y,Z. RoomOrigins in entities.Dungeon stores dungeon.Position (int). Entity positions in EncounterData use entities.Position (float64). The int/float64 mismatch requires type casts at every boundary. This is the root cause of the five coordinate-space bugs.

items.summary: dungeon_mapper.go line 44 routes crypt theme to ThemeDebugWalls
items.details: mapTheme in dungeon_mapper.go: case 'crypt' returns dungeon.ThemeDebugWalls with a TODO comment 'swap back to ThemeCrypt after wall UI testing'. This is present in the docs/honest-status-snapshot branch. All crypt dungeons show debug walls in any build from this branch.

items.summary: OpenDoor reveal stores room-B walls and entities without translating from room-local to dungeon-absolute, so revealed rooms overlap room A geometrically
items.delta: Localized to buildRoomLayoutProto in orchestrator.go (line ~1098). Entity positions and CubeEntities were already translated correctly; only RoomLayout.walls in EncounterStateData.rooms were room-local. Fix on branch fix/cross-room-state-wave2 applies origin element-wise to each wall vertex at the producer. Awaiting Kirk's playtest verification before flipping to resolved.

items.summary: Wall-collision / event-publish consumers loaded only currentRoom.Walls, missing every other revealed room's perimeter walls
items.delta: Sibling of #493: that bug was at the producer (rendering data); this one was at the consumers (collision + event data). MoveCharacter, executeMonsterTurns, ResolveAttack, executeMoveAction all loaded dungeon.GetRoom(currentRoomID).Walls and treated that as the encounter wall set. After OpenDoor revealed room B, room B's perimeter was invisible — collision passed straight through. New helper loadAbsoluteWallsForRevealedRooms (revealed_walls.go) returns the union in dungeon-absolute. Wall consumers now use this. MoveCharacter / executeMoveAction also stop translating target absolute → room-local before the wall check (consistent absolute-frame collision). executeMonsterTurns drops the per-step localToAbsoluteOrLocal on turnResult.Movement (absolute in, absolute out). Commit 44ce47f layered onto branch fix/cross-room-state-wave2. Awaiting Kirk's playtest verification.

items.summary: StreamEncounterEvents server-side handler reads as correct: looped over ctx.Done / errors-chan / events-chan with continue on convert errors; no path returns after one event by design
items.delta: Wave 2 playtest reported the browser network tab showing the gRPC-Web stream flipping pending->200 after one event. Read of internal/handlers/dnd5e/v1alpha1/encounter/handler.go:672-739: the handler loops on a select over (1) stream.Context().Done — only fires on real client disconnect, (2) subOutput.Errors — fires on initial Redis Receive failure or unmarshal error in the listen goroutine; treated as fatal and returns codes.Internal, (3) subOutput.Events with `continue` on convertToProtoEvent error and `return sendErr` only on stream.Send failure. No code path returns nil/success after exactly one event. The Subscribe call uses a subCtx derived from context.Background (not the handler ctx), so internal subscription lifetime is not tied to the gRPC ctx; only Unsubscribe (in the handler defer) cancels it. The Redis publisher's listen goroutine in internal/publishers/encounter/redis.go:182-232 ranges msgChan until ctx cancellation, with non-blocking error forward + ctx.Done guard. Theory: real cause is one of: (a) a single unmarshal failure on a particular event type that bubbles up through subOutput.Errors and terminates the stream, (b) envoy / grpc-web proxy timing out the stream after the first frame, or (c) client-side stream cancel that the server simply observes as ctx.Done. Diagnostic [wave2-debug] logging added at every server-side decision point on commit 4443520 of fix/cross-room-state-wave2 — next playtest should distinguish (a) from (b)/(c) by which RETURN line fires.

items.summary: OpenDoor publish path emits a complete revealed-room layout in EncounterStateData.Rooms[revealedRoomID] (walls translated to absolute, width/height/grid/origin set); no obvious server-side regression
items.delta: Wave 2 playtest reported no room appearing on OpenDoor after commit 44ce47f, when it had appeared after 5771c96. Read of OpenDoor in internal/orchestrators/encounter/orchestrator.go:3029-3487: step 10 marks RevealedRooms[revealedRoomID]=true via dungeonRepo.Update; step 11 persists the combined RoomData and Entities; step 16 builds revealedSpatialRoom; the snapshot at line 3457 calls buildEncounterStateSnapshot which reloads the dungeon (now containing the just-marked room) and calls buildRoomsMap (orchestrator.go:1185-1212) which iterates dng.RevealedRooms and produces *pb.RoomLayout for every revealed room via buildRoomLayoutProto (orchestrator.go:1110-1182), translating walls to dungeon-absolute via origin element-wise add and setting width/height/grid/origin on every layout. The published RoomRevealedEvent then carries the snapshot in event.RoomRevealed.EncounterStateData (handler.go:1119-1125 maps it to proto). 44ce47f did not touch the OpenDoor publish path; it only changed wall consumers in MoveCharacter / executeMoveAction / executeMonsterTurns / ResolveAttack and added loadAbsoluteWallsForRevealedRooms. So the OpenDoor server-side emission should still produce the same complete layout. If the web client really is rendering nothing on OpenDoor, the bug is more likely (a) the stream is closed before the RoomRevealed event arrives (see disc-stream-lifecycle), or (b) the web client changed how it consumes EncounterStateData.Rooms[revealedRoomID] vs the response shape returned by the OpenDoor RPC. Diagnostic [wave2-debug] logging added on commit 4443520 to verify the snapshot's Rooms.keys, RevealedRoomIds, and the revealed room's wall/dimension/origin fields just before publish — the next playtest produces conclusive evidence.

items.summary: OpenDoor zeroed the active turn's MovementRemaining (and ActionEconomy) in the response/event/snapshot by constructing a fresh CombatState without copying those fields from the persisted encounter data
items.delta: Wave 2 playtest: 'when I opened the door I had like 3 spaces left. when I open the door my range becomes 0 and the border disappears.' Read of OpenDoor in internal/orchestrators/encounter/orchestrator.go showed it builds a CombatState literal at line 3377 with EncounterID/TurnOrder/ActiveIndex/Round/CombatStarted only — MovementRemaining and ActionEconomy default to zero. That CombatState is returned in OpenDoorOutput (line 3492), published in RoomRevealedEvent (line 3478), and handed to buildEncounterStateSnapshot (line 3457) for the snapshot proto. Server-side persisted MovementRemaining is never mutated by OpenDoor (grep confirmed: no writes to encOutput.Data.MovementRemaining or to encounterrepo.UpdateInput.MovementRemaining anywhere in OpenDoor). So this was a pure response/event/snapshot serialization bug, not a state mutation. Fix: copy encOutput.Data.MovementRemaining and encOutput.Data.ActionEconomy into the constructed CombatState. Mirrors what buildCombatState already does for every other call site (orchestrator.go:2295-2313). Regression test TestOpenDoor_PreservesMovementBudget asserts both the response.CombatState carries forward the budget AND that the encounter UpdateInput leaves MovementRemaining/ActionEconomy nil (i.e. OpenDoor doesn't write them). Test fails on the parent commit (expected: 25, actual: 0) and passes after the fix. Awaiting Kirk's playtest verification.

items.summary: Player-move events appear to never reach the web client visually; investigation pinpoints fix is web-side, API publish path is intact
items.delta: Bug reported on Wave 2 playtest (and confirmed on main, not a Wave 2 regression). MoveCharacter accepts the request and returns success. Monster pathing/attack/death events DO arrive on the client. Player-move events visibly do not move the character. Traced the publish chain end-to-end: orchestrator.go:1846 publishes MovementCompletedEvent with UpdatedEntity (built from encOutput.Data.Entities[entityID] at line 1803-1819) and CombatStateProto (always built). entities/encounter_events_json.go:261-297 wraps these json:"-" proto fields in a base64/proto-wire-format MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON shim so they survive Redis pub/sub. handler.go:948-955 maps both fields to the proto MovementCompletedEvent that ships to the client. New regression tests verify each link: TestPublishSubscribe_MovementCompleted_PreservesProtoFields (publisher-level Redis roundtrip with miniredis) and TestMoveCharacter_PublishesEventWithUpdatedEntityAndCombatState (orchestrator publishes with UpdatedEntity and CombatStateProto when Entities map is populated). Both pass. Compared to monster events: MonsterTurnCompletedEvent has Movement []dungeon.AbsolutePosition (json:"movement", JSON-preserved) which the web client uses in applyMonsterMovement (LobbyView.tsx:89-114) to update room.entities[monsterId].position. Player movement has the symmetric proto field — MovementCompletedEvent.path (handler.go:940-947 builds from FinalPosition, also JSON-preserved) — but the web client's handleMovementCompleted (LobbyView.tsx:691-706) does NOT consume event.path. It only updates state when event.updatedEntity or event.combatState is truthy. So if the API publishes correctly but updatedEntity is degraded for any reason (e.g., Entities map missing the player at move time), the player visibly stays put. Fix is on the web side: handleMovementCompleted should fall back to event.path for the entity-position update, mirroring what applyMonsterMovement does for monsters. No rpg-api code change needed; regression tests added on branch fix/cross-room-state-wave2 to pin the publish-path contract.

items.summary: Investigated hypothesized MoveCharacter parallel-to-d555fb6 bug zeroing canonical actionEconomy.movementRemaining on cross-door moves; found the orchestrator path already correct, but the handler does drop FinalPosition + StopReason on the floor in the proto response
items.delta: Wave 2 playtest log (web bd6c2db, api 9b8971f): pre-move movementRemaining=15, request path Array(4), response success=true movementRemaining=0 stopReason='', event MovementCompleted hasUpdatedEntity=true movementRemaining_canonical=0 movementMax_canonical=30. Kirk hypothesized this was the same shape as d555fb6 (OpenDoor) — a hand-rolled CombatState literal in MoveCharacter omitting MovementRemaining/ActionEconomy. Verified by reading orchestrator.go:1851-1868 and 5475-5494: both MoveCharacter and executeMove route the published MovementCompletedEvent's CombatStateProto through buildCombatState (orchestrator.go:2302-2320) which copies enc.MovementRemaining + enc.ActionEconomy correctly. New regression test TestMoveCharacter_CrossRoomMove_PreservesCanonicalMovementBudget (move_character_canonical_budget_test.go) pins the contract: 11-hex cross-door move with 60ft pre-move publishes event with canonical actionEconomy.movementRemaining=5 (60-55=5). Test passes on the parent commit 9b8971f, confirming the orchestrator path is correct. The playtest's movementRemaining=0 is consistent with consuming all 15ft (3-hex move at 5ft/hex). Real handler-level bug found: handler.go:327-330 only copies Success+MovementRemaining into the proto response — FinalPosition (proto field 3) and StopReason (proto field 5) are silently dropped. Wave 2 stopReason='' was the handler being lossy, not the orchestrator. Fixed by populating both fields from output. handler_test.go TestMoveCharacter_Success now asserts both fields propagate (fails on parent, passes after fix). MoveCharacterResponse proto does NOT carry CombatState, so the canonical movement value flows only via the MovementCompletedEvent — the orchestrator already handles that correctly.

items.summary: Revealed room missing perimeter walls (interior walls render, perimeter doesn't) — proven API-innocent; cause is web-side rendering
items.delta: Wave 2 playtest after the four web fixes + 5771c96 + 44ce47f + 4443520 + d555fb6: door opens, room B floor renders, monster comes toward player, but revealed room shows interior walls without outer/perimeter walls. Earlier debug log: '[wave2-debug] OpenDoor revealed-room layout ... walls=21 origin=y:-17 z:17'. Walked the producer chain end to end: components/dungeon/generator.go:271,431 calls updateRoomPerimeters on every room (every room, not just start), which generates 5-6 perimeter_* walls per shape. components/dungeon/generator.go:355-362 sets room.Walls = append(perimeterWalls, featureWalls...) so dungeon.Room.Walls always carries both. Confirmed empirically by spawning a real generator run across 7 seeds × Theme{Crypt, DebugWalls} × 4 rooms — every room has perim=5 or 6, none missing. orchestrators/encounter/orchestrator.go:1110 buildRoomLayoutProto iterates every wall in room.Walls and emits each with origin element-wise added — perimeter and interior walls go through the same code path, no filter. orchestrators/encounter/orchestrator.go:1185 buildRoomsMap iterates dng.RevealedRooms and produces a layout for every revealed room. EncounterStateData.rooms[revealedRoomID].walls therefore carries the full perimeter+interior set in dungeon-absolute coords. Conclusion: rpg-api emits perimeter walls correctly; the symptom is web-side. New regression test TestBuildRoomsMap_RevealedRoom_PerimeterEnvelopePresent (build_room_layout_test.go) uses a real generated 3-room dungeon, marks every room revealed, runs buildRoomsMap, and asserts the emitted wall vertex bbox spans the room's nominal width × height in absolute coords. Test passes — perimeter walls reach the room edges. wave2_debug.go log extended with vertex bbox + perimeter/interior wall counts (material proxy) + 4 sample walls per revealed room, so the next playtest will print conclusive evidence on the wire. Cross-room attack contingency: ResolveAttack (orchestrator.go:298) finds target via findMonsterData (monster_turns.go:462), which iterates encOutput.Data.Monsters with no current-room scope; no roomID gate at handler level either. If 'cannot hit monster from new room' is real, it's web-side. Branch: fix/cross-room-state-wave2 commit 9b8971f.
